subject: Monitoring data exports & SLO exception request - Siena Analytics
messages:
From: Marcus Gilmore <marcus.gilmore@siena-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@siena-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLO evidence + monitoring export request

Hi Ben,

We’re finalizing paperwork for our security & procurement review and have a few follow-ups on the SLOs you listed in the draft contract. Could you confirm the following so our compliance team can close their checklist?

1) Measurement windows — For the 99.9% uptime SLO, what is the exact rolling window you use (30d, 90d, calendar month)? How do you treat planned maintenance windows?

2) Alerting — Which alerts are cross-account (i.e., customers get routed alerts) vs internal-only? Can we get an example of the PagerDuty/ops workflow for a regional outage?

3) Metric definitions — We need a canonical mapping from the SLO name to metric name and query (e.g., error budget burn = sum(rate(errors[5m])) / sum(rate(requests[5m])).

4) Historical exports — procurement asked for a 6-month export showing uptime and p99 latency for our closest region (us-west). Can you provide a CSV or a read-only dashboard link?

5) Exception path — If you cannot meet the SLO and we request an exception or SLA credit, what is the operational process and typical turnaround? Any prior examples (anonymized) would help.

We’re on a tight timeline; if you can send the answers and an export by EOD Tuesday 16 Feb that would keep us on track for Q1 procurement sign-off.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Gilmore
Procurement Manager, Siena Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Gilmore <marcus.gilmore@siena-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO evidence + monitoring export request

Marcus — thanks for the clear list. I’ll cover each item below and attach the exports you asked for. Looping in Neha (SRE) for the measurement queries and Laura for contract/exception process.

1) Measurement windows: We calculate SLOs on a 30-day rolling window by default; we also provide a 90-day view for trending. Planned maintenance is excluded if scheduled and announced at least 48 hours in advance and marked in our maintenance calendar — otherwise it counts against the SLO. We can provide calendarized maintenance records for the last 6 months.

2) Alerting: Customer-facing alerts are limited to high-impact incidents (regional outage or sustained service degradation). Those are escalated via PagerDuty to the on-call and mirrored to a read-only incident channel we can grant you access to. Internal-only alerts (degraded KPIs, skews in model latency under load) are routed to SRE triage and not forwarded to customers automatically. We’ll include an anonymized PD playbook in the attachment.

3) Metric definitions: Attached is a matrix (slo_definition_matrix.pdf) that maps SLO names to Grafana queries and Prometheus metric names. Example (p99 latency): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) filtered by region and model_family.

4) Historical exports: I’ve exported 6 months of daily aggregates for us-west (uptime, p50/p90/p99 latency) into metrics_export_20270214.csv. I’ve also created a read-only Grafana link — you can find it in related_links below. If you need raw per-request logs for deeper analysis we can discuss an NDAs-backed export.

(attachment: metrics_export_20270214.csv)
(attachment: slo_definition_matrix.pdf)

5) Exception path: Our exception process is documented in the mutual action plan link and summarized here: you submit a formal request (Doc + justification) → SRE review (48–72 hrs) → if approved, we create a scoped exception with duration and compensating controls (e.g., increased monitoring, SLA credits if agreed). Typical turnaround for a standard review is 3 business days; for complex cross-region impacts it can take up to 10 business days. For manufacturing-level safety cases we’ve done expedited reviews in 24–48 hrs. Laura, can you add standard contract language for exceptions?

I’m sending the exports now and will follow up with a short screen share to walk the SRE playbook if useful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: grafana-invite.txt)
From: Marcus Gilmore <marcus.gilmore@siena-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 07:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO evidence + monitoring export request

Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the files. Quick clarifications after a first pass through the CSV and matrix:

• The CSV has daily aggregates; procurement specifically asked for event-level failures for two outage windows (Nov 16 and Dec 3). Can you provide the 48-hour event dumps for those dates (anonymized IDs fine)?

• On planned maintenance — we need a defined SLA for emergency maintenance that might be scheduled with less than 48 hours. Is there a clause we can add for emergent maintenance windows so those aren’t automatically counted against uptime if both parties agree?

• Exception credits — we need an illustration of how credits are calculated for partial-outages (e.g., 10% degradation across a subset of endpoints). Is that in the contract appendix or do we need a separate schedule?

Also, can you send the Grafana read-only invite to procurement@ for our dashboard reviewers?

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Gilmore <marcus.gilmore@siena-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@siena-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO evidence + monitoring export request

Marcus — thanks, good questions. Short answers and next steps below.

• Event-level dumps: We can provide anonymized 48-hour event-level exports for Nov 16 and Dec 3. Security requires a signed export agreement (NDA addendum); I’ve attached a one-page export agreement template and included the CSV of the daily aggregates you already saw. If you sign the addendum we’ll push the event dumps to a secure bucket (S3 presigned link) within 24 business hours.

• Emergent maintenance clause: We can add a mutually-agreed emergent maintenance clause to the contract — essentially an exception process that requires written notice to procurement@ and a documented post-event review. Laura will propose language and a timeline for approvals; she’s copied here.

• Credit calculation: We maintain a standard credit schedule in the SLA appendix that describes prorated credits by percentage of affected traffic and duration. I’ve pasted a short worked example in the attachment and Laura will add the formal schedule to the contract doc.

Next steps:
- I’ll send the Grafana read-only invite to procurement@ and marcus (should arrive shortly).
- Laura will drop proposed contract language for emergent maintenance and the credit schedule by EOD Thursday 18 Feb.
- If you sign the export addendum we’ll deliver the two event-level dumps.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you’d rather review the export and exception language together.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | developer-first LLM inference
(attachment: export-agreement-nda-addendum.pdf)
